brief: Nomura's McElligott frames the 2.6% overnight Emini round-trip (7,630 to 7,490 to 7,687, after Trump told Fox he hopes not to veto Democrats) as mostly mechanical. Tail hedges and monetized puts from the blue-tsunami selloff became rally fuel, with client flow rotating into capped call spreads rather than naked calls. The narrative layer argues a Democratic Congress will brake AI capex, deficits, Iran and wealth-tax risk at once. On datacenters: a belief that the election results force buildout moderation eases financing, FCF-burn and UST crowding-out fears, since no single hyperscaler could cut capex alone but a Democratic governor can. Texas holds 26.7% and Democrat-restricted states roughly 45% of planned US capacity, potentially pushing some 2027 gigawatts into 2028. McElligott's twist: Big Tech pre-empted this by co-drafting a national datacenter framework with the Sierra Club, League of Conservation Voters and NRDC, which could let a Democratic administration slow rather than freeze buildout, though debt issuance (Meta's $15 billion dollar deal, a new euro raise) stays robust. Gold's 2.9% jump signals both a debasement trade against future deficit spending and easing GCC/Iran bullion-selling pressure. McElligott concludes rates stay two-way, not a duration buy, and the piece notes that since hedge-unwind is the only mechanical driver and it runs out, the narrative-moderation bid may already be fading, as Nasdaq futures turned negative.
